headline: Mild, dry Thursday, then a wet, windy stretch from Friday into early next week.
summary: A warm front brought mild air, and a cold front has stalled offshore. Thursday stays mostly dry and pleasant, with highs in the lower 60s and possibly a Seattle record. Then a deep low-pressure system heads toward Washington Friday, followed by a strong Pacific front Saturday. An upper-level dip keeps things unsettled through Sunday, with showers into Monday. Friday brings widespread rain and gusty winds, strongest on the coast and in mountain gaps. Saturday looks wetter and windier, with the worst gusts on the coast. High tides could bring minor coastal flooding Friday morning, and heavy Olympic rain may keep the Skokomish River high. Forecasters are fairly sure of a wet, windy stretch, but small shifts in storm tracks would change where the strongest winds and rain land.
changes: Since the afternoon update, the wind threat for Saturday is more specific, with gusts of 40 mph or more possible on the coast. A gale warning for coastal waters is now likely, and Thursday is now expected to be a possible record-warm day in Seattle.
